prompt: Simplify: $(x^3)^2 \cdot x^4 \div x^5$. Write your answer as a power of $x$.
hint: Three exponent rules are needed here. Take them one at a time, starting with the power of a power.

hints.text: Three exponent rules are needed here. Take them one at a time, starting with the power of a power.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Do one rule at a time. First $(x^3)^2 = x^6$ (multiply the exponents). Now it is just $x^6 \cdot x^4 \div x^5$.
$(x^3)^2 = x^6$. Then multiply by adding exponents: $x^6 \cdot x^4 = x^{10}$. Last, divide by subtracting the exponent $5$.
$x^{10} \div x^5 = x^{10-5}$, so the expression simplifies to $x^5$.

explanation: Use the power rule first and multiply the exponents: $(x^3)^2 = x^6$.
Use the product rule next and add the exponents: $x^6 \cdot x^4 = x^{10}$.
Use the quotient rule last and subtract the exponents: $x^{10} \div x^5 = x^5$, so the answer is $x^5$.

alternativeExplanations.title: One running count of copies
steps: Count copies of x from left to right: the square of x³ gives 6 copies, then +4 more makes 10.
Dividing by x⁵ erases 5 copies: 10 − 5 = 5 copies left, so x⁵.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test with real numbers
steps: Let x = 2. (2³)² = 64, times 2⁴ = 16 gives 1024. Divide by 2⁵ = 32: 1024 ÷ 32 = 32.
32 = 2⁵, so the simplified form is x⁵.
